events.name: Southern California Santa Ana windstorm
events.region: Los Angeles and Ventura counties, Southern California
events.headline: A strong offshore wind event with gusts of 70–90 mph in the mountains, humidity near 10% and coastal heat in the 90s. It peaked on 16 October and eases from 18 October, ahead of a cooler storm system expected around 21–22 October.

events.name: Typhoon Champi
events.region: Western Pacific · Guam, Taiwan, Ryukyus, eastern China, Japan
events.headline: Champi passed within 12 miles of Guam's southern tip on 18 October with its core of extreme winds mostly offshore, then became a super typhoon over the Philippine Sea and reached 159 kt (183 mph, 1-minute) on 20 October in JTWC's provisional best track, the highest winds of 2026 worldwide so far and 5 kt above Sinlaku's 154 kt (177 mph) in April; press reports quoted 185 mph on 21 October. Taiwan's weather agency had expected it to turn north off Taiwan's east coast rather than make landfall; by 23 October it had passed off the northeast coast with extremely heavy rain (650 mm in Yilan since Thursday). As reported on 24 October, one person died, 616 were injured and 4,960 were evacuated in Taiwan; the counts were still changing. Rain was then forecast for eastern China, the Ryukyus, South Korea and southern Japan before the storm dissipates over Japan around 26 October.
events.as_of: 24 Oct 2026 (Taiwan Central Emergency Operation Center, 24 Oct; Al Jazeera, 23 Oct; AccuWeather update 22 Oct 16:45 UTC; Khaleej Times/Taiwan CWA 21 Oct)

events.name: Istanbul and Rhodes cloudbursts
events.headline: Istanbul's heaviest rain since records began in 1942 shut the city down; on the same day Rhodes received 202 mm in about six and a half hours. The weather system behind both has not yet been described in detail by the met services, so this entry stays open.
events.as_of: 19 Oct 2026 (death toll: Euronews, 19 Oct; rainfall and Rhodes: reports of 15–16 Oct)

events.name: Hurricane Trudy
events.headline: The third major hurricane in a month on the same stretch of Mexican coast. Trudy jumped from Category 1 to Category 3 in under nine hours on 16 October, then stalled when dry air opened its eyewall.

events.name: Southern Plains heat–flood–freeze
events.type: Stalled front: flash flood, snow, freeze
events.region: Oklahoma, West Texas, the Rockies, eastern US
events.headline: Record heat, then record moisture, then a hard freeze within a week. A front stalled across Oklahoma between two weather systems and storms trained over the same counties, dropping 4–11 in of rain and pushing the Canadian River into major flood.
events.as_of: 23 Oct 2026 (event window closed with the expiry of the Canadian and North Canadian river flood warnings, 19–20 Oct)

events.name: Budhi Gandaki flood
events.headline: ~1 km landslide at Siringe Himal dammed the Ungilung stream; breach ~04:00 11 Oct.

events.name: Lipari flash flood
events.headline: Upper trough from the west: 500 hPa heights fell 5,825 to 5,687 m.

events.name: Hurricane Simon
events.headline: Simon exploded from Category 1 to Category 4 in about 24 hours (peak 135 kt), then stalled offshore for nearly a week instead of hitting Sinaloa as forecast, battering the Jalisco–Colima–Guerrero coast and closing Puerto Vallarta airport.

events.name: Hurricane Isaias
events.headline: The first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 peaked at Category 3 over the Gulf, then hit near Destin, Florida, on 9 October as a Category 2 with 105 mph winds.

events.name: Post-tropical Rachel
events.type: Remnant storm, swell and coastal flooding
events.headline: Rachel's remnants killed at least five people in Ensenada (AP, 12–13 Oct) and sent a long-period swell onto Southern California beaches already sitting 1–2 ft above the tide tables.

events.name: Peru coastal El Niño (extraordinary)
events.headline: Kelvin waves reaching South America keep warm water against the coast.

events.name: Los Angeles high-water residual (October 2026)
events.headline: Preliminary NOAA CO-OPS observations at Los Angeles were above hourly tide predictions during 13–16 October 2026. The residual does not identify its cause; the claimed Kelvin-wave and marine-heatwave contributions are unverified.
events.as_of: 24 Oct 2026 (NOAA CO-OPS Los Angeles observations through 16 Oct checked)

events.name: Hurricane Lowell
events.headline: Category 5 on 2 Sep; ridge weakened 5 Sep and an upper low pulled it north (it passed just west of Kauai without a direct hit, on a northward track like Iniki's in 1992).

events.name: Langtang rock-ice avalanche
events.headline: ~2 km² of rock and ice fell 1,400 m from 5,150 m (energy like M5.5).

events.name: US Fourth of July heat dome
events.headline: Ridge drew humid Gulf air; lasted over a week.

events.name: Canadian wildfires
events.headline: Prolonged July heat and dryness; in the week beginning 20 July 2026 widespread lightning storms triggered numerous new fires (WWA, citing The Guardian and Reuters).

events.name: European June heatwave
events.headline: Persistent high with southerly flow from North Africa.

events.name: Record east-based El Niño
events.headline: ENSO Longitude Index 191.5°E, easternmost on record by a wide margin (previous record 178.5°E), by Daniel Swain's weekly calculation (Weather West, 12 Oct 2026): an east-based event like 1982–83 and 1997–98.

events.name: European compound summer
events.headline: Persistent alternating highs and lows (WMO).

events.name: South Asia pre-monsoon heat
events.headline: Heat built mid-April after western disturbances ended.

events.name: Western N. America heat dome
events.headline: Clear skies, sinking air; LA extreme heat warning.

events.name: Hawaiʻi Kona lows
events.headline: Back-to-back lows and upper disturbances reversed the trades.

events.name: Minas Gerais floods
events.headline: Persistent localised rain; wettest February since 1961 in Juiz de Fora.

events.name: Winter Storm Fern
events.headline: Pacific low crossed the Plains, drew Gulf moisture, re-formed as a nor'easter.

events.name: Storm Harry
events.headline: Cut-off low over Iberia stalled for a week.

events.name: Southern Africa floods
events.headline: Repeated heavy rain systems; a year's rain in days in places.
